analysis:
Reviewed the base_text of EngineV2BridgeTests.swift (units 2 and 3) alongside the patch excerpt. The file is test-only, so no production code is touched. The changes are: a decodeTable on StubTokenizer (line 146 of head), a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge helper (lines 440 and 459), and new stop-string-scope matching tests (head lines 844-896). The excerpt is truncated, so the new tests cannot be reviewed in full.

No trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage logic is modified. T-041 (prefix-cache salt scoping) is only exercised by existing tests such as bridgeStampsCacheSalt. Those tests still assert that caller-supplied prompt_cache_key and user do not become cacheSalt. Nothing here weakens that.

Open question for integration: the production EngineV2Bridge.init now takes stopStringScope, and matchedStopSequence takes a scope argument. Neither implementation is in this batch. The question is whether stop-sequence reporting could leak scoped reasoning text, which would be a minor information-disclosure concern. That cannot be judged from the test file alone. The production files should be checked: how the matched stop sequence is surfaced via EngineV2RequestUsageSignal, and whether the scope parameter correctly limits matching to the answer region.

No findings from this test-only change.
